about: Synthetic students for scripts/eval_memory.py, written for the eval: no real student data. Each has memories (check-ins, follow-up answers, chat lines; days_ago counts back from the eval's fixed date) with facts planted among look-alike distractors, and questions whose answers are memory ids. A question marked changed is about a fact the student later changed; its newer memory is listed first.

students.about: Maya is a high school junior in Easton, Ohio who spent the summer and early fall testing lead in her town's tap water and presenting it to the town council, while weighing colleges and shifting from environmental science toward public health.

memories.context: Pick your quest and write down why it matters to you
memories.body: ok starting this for real. my aunt rosa got a letter from the water dept last year saying her house might have a lead pipe and nobody on her street knew what that meant. i want to actually find out

memories.context: Read the basics of the federal Lead and Copper Rule
memories.body: read the epa summary of the lead and copper rule. the action level is 15 ppb but they also say there's no safe level for kids which is kind of terrifying. took notes on my phone

memories.context: Find where Ohio posts drinking water sampling results
memories.body: found the ohio epa drinking water watch site. it's super clunky but you can search by water system, and easton's system number is printed on our water bill which is kinda funny
hi, rising junior here. i'm pretty sure i want to major in environmental science, like doing field work outside at streams and forests, not stuck in an office all day

memories.context: Download the lead sampling results for Easton's water system
memories.body: downloaded all the lead results for easton from 2019 to 2025 as a csv. it's like 60 rows, way smaller than i expected for a whole town
heads up for planning stuff, my laptop died in june and we can't replace it rn, maybe christmas. so at home it's just my phone, and the public library computers kick you off after an hour

memories.context: Open the data and note what each column means
memories.body: went through the columns. site id, sample date, result, and the result is in mg/L not ppb which confused me for like 20 minutes. 0.015 mg/L is the same as 15 ppb
for colleges i think i want somewhere small, like under 3000 students, quiet, and no more than 2 hours from home. big schools kind of freak me out tbh

memories.context: Convert every result to ppb and sort highest to lowest
memories.body: converted everything to ppb and sorted it. highest was 41 ppb in 2022 at one site, most are under 5 which is good i guess

memories.context: Write down three questions the data can't answer
memories.body: wrote down 3 things this data can't tell me: which houses actually have lead pipes, who lives in them, and whether it's getting better or worse

memories.context: List which neighborhoods the sampling sites are in
memories.body: tried to figure out where the sites are but the data only has site ids, no addresses. so i can't tell which neighborhoods these are. kind of stuck

memories.context: List which neighborhoods the sampling sites are in
memories.body: i think i'll email the water department and ask which streets each site id is on, they have to know right

memories.context: Count how many sites were sampled each year
memories.body: counted sites per year. 2019 had 20, 2022 had 20, 2025 had 18. so they only sample every 3 years, i thought it was every year
one thing about how i work, i do way better with a checklist. i put every step on a sticky note on my mirror and peel them off when they're done. big vague tasks make me freeze up

memories.context: Compare Easton's numbers to two nearby towns
memories.body: pulled the same data for two nearby towns. one has way lower numbers but it's a much newer town. easton's 90th percentile was 9 ppb in 2022, under 15 but not by alot

memories.context: Check whether schools and the Flats show up in the state data
memories.body: big problem. none of the schools are in the state data at all, and the 4 sites i can place aren't in the flats, which is the oldest part of town. so the data might miss the places i care about most

memories.context: Write a short email to the water department asking for site locations
memories.body: drafted the email. asked which streets the sampling sites are on and if they have anything older than 2019. kept it short and polite, sending it tomorrow morning
is it weird to email a government office as a 16 year old? i need info from the water department and im scared they'll just ignore me

memories.context: Send the email and start a log of who you contacted
memories.body: sent the email this morning, fingers crossed

memories.context: Send the email and start a log of who you contacted
memories.body: i sent it to the general info address on their website since i couldn't find a real person's name, and started a contacts list in my notes

memories.context: Read about how lead gets into tap water
memories.body: read about lead service lines today

memories.context: Read about how lead gets into tap water
memories.body: it's the pipe from the water main to your house. houses built before about 1950 often have lead ones, and most of the flats is from the 1920s

memories.context: Look up when Easton's water pipes were installed
memories.body: found an old town history pdf. the water system was built in 1908 and most of the flats went up between 1915 and 1930, so lead lines there are really likely

we drove to oberlin for a summer tour yesterday and honestly i loved it. the environmental studies building has solar panels and a living machine that cleans wastewater with plants, and everyone was so nice to us

memories.context: Follow up on your email to the water department
memories.body: the water dept replied!! a guy named mr delgado, he's their water quality supervisor. he said schools aren't in the state data because they test separately, and he'll send me the site list with street names

memories.context: Set up a spreadsheet to track sites, streets and pipe material
memories.body: made the tracking sheet at the library with columns for site id, street, year built, pipe material and result. mostly empty for now but it looks official

memories.context: Read the town's annual water quality report
memories.body: read this year's water quality report

memories.context: Read the town's annual water quality report
memories.body: it says easton had zero violations, but it only gives the 90th percentile number, nothing about individual houses or streets

memories.context: Read how other towns handled their lead lines
memories.body: read about newark nj replacing basically all of its lead service lines in like 3 years, free for homeowners. so it's possible if a town actually wants to
is it better to take ap stats or ap calc senior year? people say colleges want calc but stats seems way more useful for data stuff

memories.context: Find the town's lead service line inventory
memories.body: looked for the lead service line inventory every water system had to publish by 2024. couldn't find it anywhere on the town website, which feels like it shouldn't be allowed

memories.context: Add the full site list and school results to your sheet
memories.body: mr delgado sent the full site list with streets plus the school results from the district, and a link to the inventory. gap filled: 5 of the 18 sites are in the flats, and every school is under 5 ppb except one fountain at the middle school

memories.context: Tag every site by neighborhood
memories.body: tagged every site by neighborhood. the flats sites are consistently the highest, like 3 of the top 4 readings every single round

memories.context: Write a one paragraph project summary to reuse in emails
memories.body: wrote a short paragraph about my project to paste into emails. took like 6 tries to make it not sound like a school essay

memories.context: Look up your street and the Flats in the line inventory
memories.body: went through the inventory, it's a giant pdf not a map. our street says galvanized requiring replacement which i had to google, and aunt rosa's whole block is listed as lead

fyi for planning, my mom works second shift at the hospital so every tuesday and thursday i have my little brothers from like 2:30 til she gets home around 11:30. those days are basically gone for anything else

memories.context: Decide what question your own testing will answer
memories.body: picked my question: do homes with lead service lines actually have more lead at the tap than homes with copper lines? the state data can't answer that, there's only 5 sites in the flats
money is honestly my biggest worry about college. my mom said she can maybe do 8k a year at most and i really don't want huge loans. is that even realistic for a decent school

memories.context: Figure out how many homes to test and where
memories.body: planning 25 homes, about half in the flats and half in newer parts of town. the epa guidance says to use first draw water that sat in the pipes at least 6 hours

memories.context: Research at-home lead test kits and their limits
memories.body: looked at test kits. mail in lab kits are like 30 to 40 dollars each which is way too much for 25 homes. the cheap strips are 20 dollars for 50 so going with those for now

memories.context: Estimate what the testing will cost
memories.body: added up costs: strips 20, bottles 18, maybe 10 for gas. under 50 total if nothing goes wrong, famous last words

memories.context: Write a sign-up form for volunteer homes
memories.body: made a google form for volunteers. asks address, year the house was built, pipe type if they know it, and a good time for pickup. kept it to 5 questions

memories.context: Post the sign-up form where neighbors will see it
memories.body: posted the form in the easton community facebook group and the flats neighborhood group. 9 sign ups in the first few hours which is way more then i expected

random but i really hate presenting. my voice shakes and i talk way too fast, and last year in bio i blanked in the middle of a slide and just stood there. the council part of this quest scares me the most

memories.context: Recruit more volunteers from the Flats
memories.body: aunt rosa put my flyer by the register at the bakery and a bunch of flats people signed up. i'm at 25 homes now, 13 in the flats and 12 in newer areas

memories.context: Order the test kits and sample bottles
memories.body: ordered the test kits and 40 sample bottles, should come friday. my mom put it on her card and i'm paying her back out of my bakery money

memories.context: Write sampling instructions for volunteers
memories.body: wrote the instructions for volunteers today

memories.context: Write sampling instructions for volunteers
memories.body: don't run any water for 6 hours, then first thing in the morning fill the bottle from the kitchen cold tap and write the time on the label
also i work saturday mornings at my aunt rosa's bakery, 6am to noon, so on saturdays i can't do anything til the afternoon and i'm usually wiped after

memories.context: Plan a route to drop off and pick up bottles
memories.body: planned the pickup route. problem is i don't have my license yet, so i'll bike to the flats houses and my mom has to drive me to the far ones on sunday since that's her only day off

memories.context: Test the first batch of samples with the strips
memories.body: tested a pilot batch of 8 samples from our house, aunt rosa's and a few neighbors, and every single strip turned positive, even the bottled water i used as a control. so either everything is bad or the strips are garbage

memories.context: Test the first batch of samples with the strips
memories.body: the box sat in my mom's hot car for two days before i opened it and it says store below 80 degrees, so probably that

memories.context: Ask Mr. Delgado what kind of testing he'd trust
memories.body: asked mr delgado what kind of testing he'd trust for a project like this. he said a certified lab, and that the utility's lab sometimes runs samples for residents if you fill out their form

memories.context: Fill out the utility lab's resident sampling request
memories.body: filled out the lab's resident sampling request for 25 homes. they'll do all 25 free since it's a public project, but they only take drop offs monday to wednesday before noon

memories.context: Tell your volunteers about the switch to lab testing
memories.body: messaged all the volunteers that we're switching to real lab bottles, so they'll get a new bottle from me this week. everyone was really chill about it
what's the actual difference between early action and early decision? my friend says she's applying ed somewhere and now i feel behind even though it's a year away

memories.context: Hand out lab bottles to the Flats homes
memories.body: handed out lab bottles to all 13 flats homes. two people invited me in and asked a ton of questions about their pipes, i felt like an actual scientist

memories.context: Get bottles to the rest of the volunteer homes
memories.body: got bottles to the other 12 homes. one lady thought i was selling something lol. all 25 have bottles now

memories.context: Remind volunteers about sampling day
memories.body: texted everyone the reminder for tomorrow: no water for 6 hours, first thing in the morning, cold tap, fill to the line

memories.context: Collect the first samples and log collection times
memories.body: picked up 12 samples and logged the time from each label. took a picture of every label on my phone so i don't mix anything up

memories.context: Get the samples to the lab
memories.body: got 23 of 25 samples into the lab. two homes forgot so they're doing it this week. the lab tech showed me the machine that measures the lead which was cool
my friend priya's sister goes to oberlin and she said the dining hall food is kinda bad lol. do people actually pick colleges based on food

memories.context: Write down what you'll do while you wait for results
memories.body: made a list for the waiting week

memories.context: Write down what you'll do while you wait for results
memories.body: clean up the sheet, read how other students presented to their town councils, and get the last two samples from the homes that forgot

memories.context: Collect the two late samples
memories.body: picked up the last 2 samples, they're in our fridge labeled do not drink lol. they go to the lab monday with the form

we were in columbus yesterday for my cousin's graduation party and walked through ohio state's public health building. undergrads were running actual water samples in a lab, i didn't know freshmen could do that

memories.context: Read about lead's health effects on kids
memories.body: read the cdc page on lead and kids. it can lower iq and attention and the damage is basically permanent. the flats has a lot of young families which makes this feel way more real

memories.context: Find out what the county health department offers
memories.body: called the county health department. the public health nurse said blood lead tests for kids under 6 are free at their clinic. saving that for the slides

ok so my plan is changing. i was all in on environmental science but the part of this project that gets me is what lead does to little kids. i think i want public health now, like environmental health or epidemiology

memories.context: Tell a teacher about the project and ask for help
memories.body: told my apes teacher ms okafor about the project and she got really into it. she said she'll help me with the stats and i can use her room after school on wednesdays
school started so i can use the library computers at lunch and in study hall now, way better than the 1 hour limit at the public library. still only my phone at home though

memories.context: Clean up the tracking sheet before results arrive
memories.body: cleaned up the whole tracking sheet today

memories.context: Clean up the tracking sheet before results arrive
memories.body: deleted duplicate rows, fixed street names that were spelled three different ways, and added the pipe type from the inventory for every home

memories.context: Learn the difference between mean and median
memories.body: watched a khan academy video on mean vs median and why one weird house can wreck an average. did the practice problems on my phone

memories.context: Enter the lab results into your sheet
memories.body: lab results came back!! they actually make sense unlike the strips. 19 homes under 5 ppb, 6 over 15, and all 6 are in the flats on lead lines. the bottled water control was zero

memories.context: Let the six high homes know their results
memories.body: the utility has to notify the 6 high homes officially but i can too, so i wrote each family a short note with their number and the info about free blood tests for kids

memories.context: Compare lead line homes to copper line homes
memories.body: compared them at lunch. lead line homes averaged 14 ppb and copper ones averaged 2. ms okafor showed me how to run a t test and the difference is significant
should i actually study for the psat in october or just take it cold? people keep saying national merit but idk what it actually does

memories.context: Make charts of your results
memories.body: made two charts, a bar chart by neighborhood and a dot plot of every home. ms okafor said the dot plot is clearer because you can actually see the 6 high ones

memories.context: Find out how to get on the town council agenda
memories.body: council meets the second monday of the month at 6:30. you get 5 minutes in public comment or you can ask the clerk for an agenda slot, so i emailed the clerk

ok i changed my mind on the small school thing. after seeing the osu labs i want a big research university where undergrads can get into real labs, and a city sounds fun now. being far from home matters less than i thought

memories.context: Write the main message of your talk in one sentence
memories.body: my one sentence: homes in the flats with lead service lines have way more lead at the tap, so the town should replace those lines first

memories.context: Outline the slides
memories.body: outlined 6 slides: why i started, the data gap, how i tested, results, what it means for kids, and my ask. moved them around til it flowed

memories.context: Draft the slides
memories.body: drafted the slides at lunch and in study hall. kept the words short and used the dot plot and a map of the flats. ms okafor said less words more pictures
is michigan too big of a reach for me? my counselor said it's really hard to get in from out of state. it's kind of my dream school though, the campus looks unreal in pictures

memories.context: Have someone who knows the data check your slides
memories.body: sent the slides to mr delgado to check my numbers. he caught one thing, the 15 ppb action level applies to the 90th percentile of the whole system, not single homes, so i reworded that slide

memories.context: Practice the talk once start to finish
memories.body: practiced it once, it was bad

memories.context: Practice the talk once start to finish
memories.body: it went 8 minutes when i only get 5, the background part alone took like 3 minutes

did the net price calculators with my mom today. michigan came out around 34k a year for us which is impossible. ohio state was about 11k. oberlin said 16k, way lower than the sticker price, so honestly it's back on my list

memories.context: Cut the talk down to five minutes
memories.body: cut most of the background and merged the data gap slide into the first one. down to 5:40, need to lose about 40 more seconds somewhere

memories.context: Practice in front of someone and get feedback
memories.body: practiced for ms okafor after school. she said i rush when i'm nervous so i should pause after every number, and use note cards instead of reading off the slides. got it to 4:50

memories.context: Make note cards for the talk
memories.body: made my note cards for monday tonight

memories.context: Make note cards for the talk
memories.body: one card per slide with just 3 or 4 words in big letters, so i can glance down instead of reading the slides

memories.context: Confirm your agenda slot and what to bring
memories.body: the clerk confirmed i'm on the agenda monday under public comment, 5 minutes. i have to bring the slides on a usb because they don't allow links

memories.context: Do a final run-through with your note cards
memories.body: final run through with the note cards. my brothers were my audience and mostly asked if the water turns people into zombies lol
should i put this water project on my common app activities list even though it's not a club or anything? it's the thing i've spent the most time on this year

memories.context: Present your findings at the town council meeting
memories.body: presented to the council tonight!! it went ok. i rushed the middle like always and ran out of time before my ask slide, but the note cards saved me when i blanked. two council members asked follow up questions

memories.context: Present your findings at the town council meeting
memories.body: one asked how many lead lines are left in the flats and another asked what families can do right now, so i said filters and the free blood tests for little kids

memories.context: Send thank-you notes after the meeting
memories.body: sent the thank you emails today

memories.context: Send thank-you notes after the meeting
memories.body: to the two council members who asked questions, the clerk, and the three volunteers who came to watch

memories.context: Follow up with the town clerk after the meeting
memories.body: emailed the clerk to follow up and she said the mayor wants a 2 page summary of my results to put on the town website. kind of huge. it's due in 3 weeks
should i ask ms okafor for a rec letter now or wait til spring? she's the teacher who knows me best because of this project

memories.context: Read the meeting minutes and note what the council decided
memories.body: read the minutes. the council asked the utility to come back with a plan to replace lead lines that starts with the flats. i literally screamed

memories.context: Look for other groups who should hear your results
memories.body: was going to email the county health department but the health commissioner emailed me first!! she saw the council video and invited me to present to the board of health in november, 10 minutes plus questions. i said yes before i could chicken out
is it bad that i spend more time on the water thing than my actual homework? my english grade dropped to a b minus and my mom noticed

memories.context: Tell all your volunteers what happened at council
memories.body: emailed all 25 volunteer homes about what happened at council and what the utility has to do next. a few replied thank you which made my whole day

memories.context: Share the results with the neighborhood
memories.body: posted a summary in the flats facebook group with the free blood test info. like 40 comments, mostly nice, one guy says i'm fearmongering
my mom asked me how the fafsa even works since she's never done one. i know it's not until next fall for me but she's already stressed about the money side

memories.context: Ask volunteers if they want to stay in the loop
memories.body: asked the volunteers if they want updates when the utility's plan comes out. 17 said yes so i made a little email list
should my college essay be about the water project? i feel like everyone writes about their big project and it might be cliche

memories.context: Ask the utility when the replacement plan is due
memories.body: asked the utility when their replacement plan goes back to council. they said january, so i put a reminder in my phone

memories.context: Write down what you'd do differently next time
memories.body: if i did this again i'd start recruiting homes way earlier and ask for the agenda slot sooner. everything at the end felt rushed
can you give me a rough plan for what i should be doing for college stuff this fall and winter? i keep hearing different things from everyone

memories.context: Write down your three biggest takeaways
memories.body: three takeaways: public data has gaps, adults actually answer emails from teenagers, and a dot plot beats a paragraph every time

students.about: Dev is a New Jersey high school senior applying for computer science (maybe economics) who works shifts at his parents' convenience store, codes on a locked-down school Chromebook through GitHub Codespaces, and is building a club-scheduling web app his school's clubs actually use.

memories.body: hey. rising senior, want to do cs, maybe econ. my parents went to college in india so this whole us application thing is new for all of us. mostly i just dont want to mess it up

memories.context: Message five club presidents about how they plan meetings
memories.body: dmed 5 club presidents on insta asking how they plan meetings. 3 answered already. every club uses something different, groupme, google cal, and one literally uses the whiteboard outside room 214

memories.context: Interview two club leads about what goes wrong with scheduling
memories.body: facetimed marcus (robotics captain) and the key club president. both said the same thing, two clubs show up to the same room and somebody gets kicked out. room conflicts are the real problem

memories.context: Write down the biggest scheduling problems you heard
memories.body: wrote the list in my notes app. short one today

memories.context: Write down the biggest scheduling problems you heard
memories.body: room double booking is number one, then people not knowing a meeting got moved, then advisors having zero idea whats going on

memories.context: Pick two clubs to pilot the app
memories.body: robotics and key club are in. both big, both sick of the groupme chaos. marcus says robotics gets like 60 people during build season
fyi i work shifts at my parents convenience store, tuesdays and thursdays 4 to 10 plus sunday mornings, mostly on the register. so those days my quest stuff is gonna be tiny, im not ghosting

memories.context: Sketch the three main screens on paper
memories.body: sketched the calendar, a club page, and the new meeting form in my notebook. the calendar looks like a spreadsheet and google cal had a baby

memories.context: List what goes on each screen
memories.body: wrote out every field. meeting form needs club, room, date, start and end, and a repeats weekly box. room is a dropdown so nobody can typo it

memories.context: Show the sketches to a club lead and get feedback
memories.body: showed marcus. he said the room dropdown is the killer feature and asked if advisors could approve meetings. put that on the maybe later list
whats a realistic cs list for a 3.8 unweighted at a normal public school in jersey. i know cs is brutal everywhere, i just dont want a list of 12 lottery tickets

memories.context: Set up the project and get a hello world page running
memories.body: my only computer is the school chromebook and its locked down, cant install python or node or anything. so i made a github codespace and got flask to say hello world in the browser. we're live-ish

memories.context: Put the code on GitHub
memories.body: repo is up on github, first commits pushed

memories.context: Put the code on GitHub
memories.body: commit early and often, and dont git add . blindly bc i almost pushed my env file with the secret key in it

memories.context: Build the club list page with a Flask template
memories.body: jinja template for the club list works. pulling from a hardcoded python list for now. ugly but its real and its mine

memories.context: Learn how JavaScript fetch and promises work
memories.body: did a fetch tutorial. my python brain keeps expecting the code to just wait for the answer. async is a whole different animal
pretty sure im applying early decision to carnegie mellon. its been the dream since 9th grade, their robotics and cs stuff is literally why i got into coding. thats the plan unless you think its dumb

memories.context: Make a branch for the club page styling
memories.body: made my first real branch, changed the header, merged it back into main. nothing broke, which feels illegal

memories.context: Load the club list from an API instead of hardcoding it
memories.body: flask has a /api/clubs route returning json now and the page fetches it. felt like an actual developer for about 5 minutes

memories.context: Style the club list page
memories.body: css done for now, looks less bad

memories.context: Style the club list page
memories.body: put each club in a card with its meeting day on it, and made the header purple bc i said so

memories.context: Design the database tables on paper
memories.body: drew the tables: clubs, rooms, events, members. events points at a club and a room. no clue yet how to handle meetings that repeat every week
rutgers is my safety i guess. in state and the cs program is solid. but like 70 kids from my school go there every year, it would feel like 13th grade ngl

memories.context: Create the tables in SQLite from a Python script
memories.body: tables created with a python script and seeded with fake clubs like the underwater basket weaving society. sqlite is chill, zero setup

memories.context: Add a form to create a new meeting
memories.body: form posts to flask and saves the meeting. zero validation so rn you can make a meeting that ends before it starts lol

memories.context: Validate the new meeting form

students.about: Ana is a first-generation Mexican-American high school junior in Chicago who ran a bean plant light-color experiment for her regional science fair, watches her younger siblings twice a week, and is shifting from nursing toward pharmacy.

memories.context: Pick a question you can test in about six weeks
memories.body: ok i picked my question!! does the color of light change how bean plants grow. i almost did salt water on plants but light seemed cooler, and beans are cheap and grow fast

memories.context: Read two sources on how plants use different colors of light
memories.body: read about photosynthesis and chlorophyll, apparently plants soak up red and blue light the most and bounce green back, which is why leaves look green?? my mind is blown ngl. took notes in my composition notebook

hi so im new to all this college stuff, nobody in my family has applied to college before. my parents came from mexico and theyre super supportive but they dont know how any of it works, so pues where do i even start

memories.context: Write your hypothesis and name your variables
memories.body: hypothesis: if bean plants grow under blue light then they will be the tallest and healthiest bc blue helps leaves grow. independent variable is light color, dependent is height and health, controlled is water, soil and cup size

memories.context: Write a step by step procedure someone else could follow
memories.body: wrote my procedure, 11 steps. took alot longer than i thought and its so boring ngl, but if somebody else cant repeat it then it doesnt really count

memories.context: Find a real study or article that tested light color on plants
memories.body: found one on a university extension website, it was pretty short

memories.context: Find a real study or article that tested light color on plants
memories.body: it said plants under only green light got tall and skinny and kinda weak, which is the opposite of what i guessed, so now im really curious what mine will do

memories.context: Decide what you will measure and how often
memories.body: decided to measure height in cm every other day from the soil line and count leaves once a week. keeping everything in one notebook so i dont lose stuff

memories.context: Pick your light colors and a control group
memories.body: picked red, blue, green and white. white is my control bc its the closest to normal light, and green is the wild card since plants reflect it

for college i really wanna stay close to home, like UIC or somewhere i can take the pink line to. my mom would be so sad if i left, she already cries at every graduation even for people she barely knows lol

memories.context: Read your teacher's reply and adjust your plan
memories.body: ms okafor wrote back!! she was my bio teacher this year. she said use the same measuring cup to water every cup and do at least 4 plants per color, not 2, so one weird plant doesnt mess up everything. changed my plan

memories.context: Make a materials list with prices
memories.body: made my materials list: colored LED bulbs, 4 cardboard boxes, foil, 16 cups, potting soil, seeds and a timer. the colored bulbs are like $6 each at home depot which adds up fast
my counselor said not to make junior year too heavy but i signed up for honors chem, precalc and AP lang anyway. is that too much? i want colleges to see im actually trying

memories.context: Set a budget and cut your list to fit it
memories.body: my whole budget is about $30, my tia lupe gave me $20 and i have $12 left from my birthday. that has to cover bulbs, soil, cups AND the tri fold board at the end so im being cheap about everything

memories.context: Collect free materials: boxes, foil and cups
memories.body: only got the boxes today, 4 from the fruteria on the corner

memories.context: Collect free materials: boxes, foil and cups
memories.body: couldnt do more bc i had to watch my little brother and sister all day, my mom picked up an extra shift at the hotel. ill grab foil and cups from the kitchen tommorow

memories.context: Sketch the light box design before you build it
memories.body: drew the whole light box setup in my notebook first with arrows and measurements. i get stuff way better when i draw it out, and when i have to explain something i like having a drawing to point at

memories.context: Put all your research notes in one place
memories.body: we dont have a printer at home so i copied my research notes by hand into the notebook. the library prints for 15 cents a page but im not spending money on notes

memories.context: Buy the bulbs, soil and seeds
memories.body: went to home depot with my dad and got red, blue and green LED bulbs plus potting soil. no matching white one so im using a daylight bulb from our hallway. for seeds im just using frijoles from the kitchen lol

memories.context: Build the four light boxes and line them with foil
memories.body: built all 4 boxes!! lined the insides with foil so the light bounces around and cut a hole in the top of each one for the bulb. my room looks like a mad scientist lab now

memories.context: Soak the bean seeds overnight before planting
memories.body: my tia said frijoles from the kitchen might not sprout so i spent $2 on a seed packet of bush beans. soaking 48 of them in a bowl overnight

memories.context: Plant four cups per color and label every cup
memories.body: planted 16 cups, 4 per color, 3 beans in each so i can keep the strongest one. labeled them with masking tape R1, B1, G1, W1 and so on and gave each one exactly 50 ml of water

memories.context: Check the soil and keep it damp but not soaked
memories.body: checked every cup, the soil is still damp from yesterday so no water today
is it bad that i dont know what to major in yet? i like biology and i think maybe nursing. my cousin daniela is in nursing school at UIC and she makes it sound really cool, like hard but worth it

memories.context: Set a timer so every box gets 12 hours of light
memories.body: plugged all 4 boxes into a power strip with a cheap outlet timer, lights on at 7am and off at 7pm. my sister sofi is mad bc the red one glows through the cracks at night lol

memories.context: Check for sprouts and write down your first observations
memories.body: no sprouts yet, checked all 16 cups

memories.context: Check for sprouts and write down your first observations
memories.body: i poked the soil a little in a couple cups and the beans look swollen, one has a tiny white root coming out, so something is happening down there

had to go with my dad to his doctor appointment to translate again, i do that a lot for both my parents. the nurse explained his blood sugar stuff so patiently, thats kinda why nursing sounds good to me

memories.context: Record which cups sprouted first and measure them
memories.body: SPROUTS!!! the blue cups came up first, B2 is already 1.5 cm. red has 2 tiny ones, white has 3 and green has nothing yet. wrote it all in the table

memories.context: Measure every sprout from the soil line
memories.body: measured every sprout from the soil line with my ruler. blue avg 2.1 cm, white 1.8, red 1.2, green 0.4. took pics with my phone too in case something happens to the notebook

memories.context: Thin each cup down to the strongest sprout
memories.body: pulled the extra sprouts so every cup has just one plant, felt kinda mean ngl. kept the healthiest looking one in each cup

memories.context: Water every cup the same amount and check the soil
memories.body: UGH theres white fuzzy stuff growing on top of the soil in the green box cups, i think its mold?? that box stays closed and gets super humid in there. G3 looks the worst
whats even the difference between a college and a university? my friend jaz keeps saying she wants northwestern and i didnt even know that was in illinois lol

memories.context: Look up what causes mold on seedling soil
memories.body: looked it up and its probably from too much water and no air moving around. some people sprinkle cinnamon on the soil?? so random but we have canela in the kitchen so im trying it

memories.context: Fix the mold and restart any cups that died
memories.body: i think i fixed it!! scraped off the fuzzy top layer, sprinkled canela, cut air holes in the green box and now i only water when the top of the soil is dry. G3 died so i replanted it

memories.context: Measure all cups and note any that look sick
memories.body: blue avg 6.3 cm, white 5.8, red 4.4, green 5.1 but the green ones are skinny and kinda pale like the article said. G3 is a baby again lol
my abuela is visiting from michoacan for two weeks so the apartment is packed lol. she saw my light boxes and thinks its brujeria, i tried explaining photosynthesis in spanish and totally failed

memories.context: Take photos of every cup from the same spot
memories.body: took photos of all 16 cups from the same spot on my dresser with the ruler next to each one, so ill have good pics for the board later

memories.context: Measure all cups and add the numbers to your table
memories.body: measured everything and added it to the table

memories.context: Measure all cups and add the numbers to your table
memories.body: the surprising part is green grew the most since last time, like 2 cm in two days, but it leans hard toward the bulb and the stem looks like a noodle
ay wait you have to PAY to apply to college?? i saw some schools want like $50 or $75 just to send the application. if i apply to 8 thats like $500 and theres no way my parents have that

memories.context: Count the leaves on every plant
memories.body: counted leaves today, blue and white have the most, red has big leaves but fewer of them. G1 fell over so i put a popsicle stick next to it to hold it up

memories.context: Measure all cups and check the leaves for spots
memories.body: measured all 16, no spots on any leaves. the blue ones are such a dark green now, they look like the plants at the store
honestly the part of the science fair im most scared of is talking to the judges. i freeze up with adults i dont know, my voice gets shaky and i forget words, even in spanish lol

memories.context: Measure all cups and look for patterns
memories.body: blue avg 9.8 cm, white 8.9, red 7.1, and green 11.2?? green is the tallest now but theyre so skinny and floppy. so tallest isnt the same as healthiest i guess

memories.context: Add a health score so height is not your only data
memories.body: made a health score from 1 to 5 for leaf color, stem thickness and if it can stand up by itself. bc height alone makes green look like the winner and it def isnt

memories.context: Measure and water all 16 cups
memories.body: measured and watered everything, took like 40 minutes

memories.context: Measure and water all 16 cups
memories.body: the blue ones have really dark green leaves and thick stems, and the red ones are getting kinda yellow on the bottom leaves, gonna keep an eye on that
my friend jaz said our school has a science bowl team, its like jeopardy but for science?? i kinda wanna try it in the fall. i love the bio questions but i know basically nothing about physics

memories.context: Measure all cups and compare the stems
memories.body: measured, the green stems are so thin they bend when i water them. the blue stems are thick like a pencil almost, its wild how different they look

memories.context: Measure all cups and write down anything unusual
memories.body: the red bulb burned out!! came home from my tios and the red box was completely dark, idk for how long, maybe since last night. thats gonna mess up my data

memories.context: Replace the broken bulb and note the gap in your data
memories.body: my dad drove me to home depot for a new red bulb, $6.48 out of my budget ugh. wrote in my notebook that red had no light for about a day so im being honest about it
my dad asked me how much college costs and i had no idea what to say, like is it 10 thousand? 60? he got kinda quiet after. is there a way to know what we would actually pay

memories.context: Measure all cups and compare this week to last week
memories.body: this week blue grew 3.1 cm, white 2.8, green 3.5 but still floppy, and red only 1.4. red is the slowest by far

memories.context: Water, measure, and write one sentence about what you see
memories.body: done, everything looks pretty normal today i think

memories.context: Water, measure, and write one sentence about what you see
memories.body: ok one thing, the white box plants have tiny flower buds already which i didnt expect this early, and the blue ones are still the darkest green

ok plot twist, i think i want pharmacy not nursing. i went to walgreens to translate for my dad and the pharmacist explained how his metformin works and why he takes it with food and i was like wait que cool

memories.context: Check soil moisture before you water
memories.body: checked every cup with my finger first and only watered 5 of them, the rest were still damp. plants look good

memories.context: Measure all cups
memories.body: measured super fast bc we had a family party at my tios house, got home at like 11 and still did it lol

memories.context: Take your final measurements and look at the roots
memories.body: last measuring day!! pulled one plant from each color to look at the roots and blue had the biggest roots by far. kinda sad to end this part ngl
do colleges care that i only have like 2 activities? its just this science fair and helping with the kids program at my church on sundays

memories.context: Put every measurement into one data table
memories.body: typed all my measurements into a google sheet on my school chromebook, took forever bc my handwriting in the notebook is a mess. 16 plants times like 5 weeks

memories.context: Find the average height for each color
memories.body: did the averages with the AVERAGE formula, i didnt know sheets could do that. final avg: green 18.9 cm, blue 17.4, white 16.1, red 12.2

memories.context: Check your data table for mistakes
memories.body: found 3 spots where i typed 1.2 instead of 12, fixed them by checking my photos. so glad i took pics of everything

school started today, junior year!! and now every tuesday and thursday i pick up my little brother mateo and my sister sofi from their school at 3 and watch them till my mom gets home around 6, so on those days i do quest stuff late

memories.context: Make a bar graph of the average final height for each color
memories.body: made a bar graph in google sheets and green is the tallest bar, which looks wrong compared to how the plants actually looked lol. i need a second graph

memories.context: Graph the health scores next to the heights
memories.body: made the second graph for the health scores

memories.context: Graph the health scores next to the heights
memories.body: it shows blue had the best health score, 4.6 out of 5, and green was the worst at 2.1. so tall doesnt mean healthy, the green ones were basically stretching to find better light

went to college night at school, the loyola table was so nice and the campus by the lake looks beautiful. but its private and the lady said tuition is over 50 thousand a year?? i almost walked away lol

memories.context: Write about what went wrong and how you handled it
memories.body: wrote my what went wrong section and its almost half a page lol. tried to be honest about everything instead of hiding it

memories.context: Use a light meter to compare how bright each box was
memories.body: ms okafor let me borrow the light meter from her classroom after school. turns out the white box was like twice as bright as the red one, so brightness wasnt really controlled. big flaw i gotta mention

memories.context: Answer your original question in one sentence
memories.body: wrote my one sentence answer, took me like 5 tries

memories.context: Answer your original question in one sentence
memories.body: light color does change how bean plants grow, blue made the healthiest plants and green made the tallest but weakest ones. thats the sentence
i was looking up pharmacy programs and butler university in indianapolis has one you get into straight from high school, 6 years and you come out a doctor of pharmacy?? im kinda obsessed now

memories.context: Write your conclusion in three sentences
memories.body: conclusion: blue light made the healthiest plants with the thickest stems and biggest roots. green made the tallest plants but they were weak bc they stretched. my hypothesis was half right
my counselor mr castillo said i can probably get fee waivers for my applications bc i get free lunch?? i didnt even know that was a thing, i was lowkey panicking about the money part

memories.context: Write your limitations and what you'd change next time
memories.body: limitations: brightness wasnt the same in every box and 4 cups per color is kinda small. next time id measure brightness before i start anything

memories.context: Register for the regional science fair
memories.body: registered for the regional fair online!! theres a $15 entry fee but the main office said the school pays it for students, thank god

memories.context: Plan the board layout on paper first
memories.body: sketched the board layout on paper, question and hypothesis on the left, setup and procedure in the middle, graphs and conclusion on the right
told my cousin daniela im going for pharmacy now instead of nursing and she wasnt even mad lol. she said at her clinicals the pharmacists are the ones everybody runs to with questions about meds

memories.context: Buy the tri-fold board and supplies
memories.body: got the tri fold board at dollar tree for like $2?? thought itd be way more. plus glue sticks and letter stickers, so im officially out of budget money lol

memories.context: Write a short abstract, 250 words or less
memories.body: wrote the abstract, its 212 words total

memories.context: Write a short abstract, 250 words or less
memories.body: the hardest part was fitting the brightness problem in without making the whole project sound bad, so i put it in one sentence at the end
can i put the science fair on my college apps even if i dont win anything? its kinda the only big thing ive done outside of class

memories.context: Draw the setup diagram for the board
memories.body: drew the setup diagram with colored pencils, the 4 boxes with the bulbs and cups inside and labels on everything. honestly its my favorite part of the board

memories.context: Write the title and a short summary for the top of the board
memories.body: title is 'Seeing Red (and Blue): How Light Color Changes Bean Plant Growth'. my sister sofi helped me pick it and now she thinks shes a scientist lol

ok update on the college thing, im definately open to going farther now, even out of state. my cousin said living in the dorms made her grow up a lot, and my mom said if its the right program we'll figure it out

memories.context: Pick your best photos and write captions
memories.body: picked 6 photos, one from each week, and wrote short captions like 'week 3: green starts leaning toward the bulb'. the popsicle stick one is kinda funny

memories.context: Make the graphs easy to read from a few feet away
memories.body: made the labels bigger and colored the bars to match the actual light colors. ms okafor looked at them in class and said to add units and error bars, had to google what error bars even are

daniela sent me a link about UIC's GPPA program, if you get in as a freshman you get a guaranteed spot in their pharmacy school later as long as you keep your grades up. that sounds way less scary than applying twice

memories.context: Print the graphs, photos and title
memories.body: printed everything at the library by my house, color is 25 cents a page so it came to $3.75. the librarian helped me fix the sizing. not having a printer at home is so annoying

memories.context: Glue everything onto the board
memories.body: glued everything on, the board is mostly DONE

memories.context: Glue everything onto the board
memories.body: i drew light pencil lines with a ruler so everything is straight this time, and the letter stickers for the title took forever but they look really clean
my english teacher mr brennan wants a personal narrative and i have no idea what to write about. is it wierd to write about translating for my parents at appointments since i was like 10

memories.context: Look at the board from across the room and fix what's hard to read
memories.body: stood across my room and looked at the board, the graphs are readable but the conclusion font was too small so i rewrote it bigger with a marker

memories.context: Write and time a 3 minute talk that follows the board
memories.body: wrote my talk on 6 notecards, it goes left to right across the board so i can point at each part. first try was 3:50 so i cut the part about building the boxes and now its 3:05

memories.context: Practice answering questions a judge might ask
memories.body: my tia lupe pretended to be a judge and asked why bush beans and why only 4 cups per color. i froze on the second one but then pointed at my setup drawing and it came back to me

memories.context: Pack everything you need for fair day
memories.body: packed the board, my notecards, one plant from each color in a box so people can see the real thing, and tape just in case. cant believe its tommorow

memories.context: Present your project at the regional science fair
memories.body: FAIR DAY!!! got 2nd place in plant science and the top 2 go to state in april!! my mom cried and kept saying esa es mi hija to random people lol

memories.context: Write a reflection on what went well and what you'd change
memories.body: reflection: if i did it again id use more cups per color, measure brightness before starting, and start the board a week earlier so im not rushing at the end

memories.context: Decide what to change for the state fair
memories.body: for state im doing a round 2 with 8 cups per color instead of 4, and matching the brightness in every box before i plant anything
now that the fair is done i wanna try science bowl for real. jaz says they meet after school twice a week and theres a big competition in february, i just gotta learn some physics lol

memories.context: Make a round 2 materials list that fits your budget
memories.body: round 2 list: 32 cups, more soil, a new seed packet and extra foil. i still have the boxes and bulbs so its only like $12 this time, and tia lupe said shell help again
honors chem is kicking my butt, everyone seems to get the unit conversions and im so lost. is it bad if i end up with a B in an honors class?

memories.context: Match the brightness in all four boxes before planting
memories.body: used the light meter again and moved the white bulb higher and the red one lower until all 4 boxes read about the same. took forever but now its actually fair

memories.context: Plant round 2 with eight cups per color
memories.body: planted all 32 cups for round 2!! took like 2 hours and my back hurts lol. labeled them R1 to R8, B1 to B8 and so on with masking tape again
my mom wants to do a little carne asada bc i got 2nd place lol. mateo already told his whole class his sister is a scientist and sofi wants to do a science fair now too

memories.context: Keep the round 2 soil damp but not soaked
memories.body: checked all 32 cups, only watered a few

memories.context: Keep the round 2 soil damp but not soaked
memories.body: i only watered the ones that looked dry on top, and i turned all the labels to face out becuase i kept having to spin the cups to read them

memories.context: Start a new data sheet for round 2
memories.body: made a new data sheet on my chromebook for round 2 with all 32 cups, and color coded the rows by light color so its easier to read
what should i be doing this year to get ready to apply next fall? is there like a checklist for juniors, bc i dont wanna miss something just bc nobody in my family did this before

memories.context: Check the round 2 cups for sprouts
memories.body: no sprouts yet but its only been 3 days

memories.context: Check the round 2 cups for sprouts
memories.body: i dug a little in B4 and the bean is swollen with a tiny root, so i think tomorrow or the day after well see the first ones

memories.context: Measure the first round 2 sprouts
memories.body: first round 2 sprouts!! 5 blue cups and 2 white ones came up, nothing in red or green yet. blue is first again just like last time
a college rep from depaul came to our school today, she was really nice but when i asked about pharmacy she said they dont have a pharmacy school, so probably not for me
